papers.summary_en: Modern cloud platforms increasingly combine strong software isolation mechanisms with shared hardware resources to improve performance and resource efficiency. Conventional containers do this by sharing the host kernel directly, whereas sandboxed runtimes (e.g., gVisor) and VM-based runtimes (e.g., Kata, QEMU/KVM) provide progressively stronger isolation. In all cases, when tenants access host-backed filesystem state, the host page cache can remain shared and observable.
